assertions.actual: Let B_ql be one spatial quasi-local C-star algebra with canonical unital isometric embeddings J_Lambda:B(H_Lambda)->B_ql for the admitted finite systems. Every finite background F explicitly records its interaction labels and boundary corrections. For xi in Xi_Q, the same finite-support rational configuration-Weyl label set of R-167 v1.6, put X=supp(xi) and restrict to the X-directed tail Lambda(F) contains X. Let W_(F,xi) be the corresponding finite configuration Weyl operator, periodized on periodic P_L. For f in C_c^1(R), define G_F(xi,f)=J_F(int_R f(t) alpha_t^F(W_(F,xi)) dt), where the integral is weak. No momentum or full phase-space Weyl source is added. The finite orbit t->alpha_t^F(W_xi) is strong-star continuous and has norm one. Hence it is weakly integrable against f and ||G_F(xi,f)||<=||f||_1. The locally finite toggle universe E contains every label changing a finite Hamiltonian: site activations and onsite Q3 terms, physical interaction bonds, and explicitly tagged boundary corrections. Relative to every finite seed X it has an integer shell map r_X:E->N with {e:r_X(e)<=R} finite for every R. The admitted finite-background family is directed and common-refinable: for every F,G the auxiliary union background F union G is admitted, and F->F union G and G->F union G admit finite allowed single-toggle paths through admitted intermediate backgrounds. For the seed X, all comparisons take place in the tail Lambda(F),Lambda(G) contain X. The radius-R condition is F triangle G subset {e:r_X(e)>R}: both backgrounds match the common infinite interaction pattern on the R-core, while shape-specific boundary corrections are outside that core. It does not require one shape to contain another shape's boundary toggles. Declare one common infinite interaction pattern. The all-shape filter neighborhood N_R(X) consists of backgrounds with Lambda(F) contains X that match the pattern on every label with r_X<=R. The periodic exact-Q3 backgrounds P_L used by v4.0 are in this comparison with periodized W_(P_L,xi), and for every R eventually P_L belongs to N_R(X). Equivalently, late P_L and every sufficiently advanced all-shape F have P_L triangle F subset {r_X>R}; hence the periodic path has the same all-shape limits. If F triangle G subset {e:r_X(e)>R}, insert labels through the admitted union F union G and telescope in allowed orders. Uniformity in the intermediate backgrounds gives sup_(|s|<=T)||G_F(xi,tau_s f)-G_G(xi,tau_s f)||<=sum_(e in F triangle G)w_e(xi,f,T)<=sum_(r>R)B_r(xi,f,T)->0. Thus the complete all-shape net has a unique norm limit G(xi,f) in B_ql, uniformly for |s|<=T and for both time orientations. The periodic v4.0 path has this same limit. For P_F=product_(j=1)^m G_F(xi_j,f_j), take the directed tail for X=union_j supp(xi_j). One toggle obeys w_e(P,T)<=sum_(j=1)^m w_e(xi_j,f_j,T) product_(k!=j)||f_k||_1. This is summable in e, so products are Cauchy by the same shell telescope. Finite linear combinations, adjoints and unital star-polynomials of the smears are all-shape norm Cauchy. Their limits agree with the corresponding algebraic operations on the generator limits.

assertions.actual: Define B_sp=C^*({G(xi,f):xi in the v1.6 configuration label set Xi_Q, f in C_c^1(R)}) as a unital C-star subalgebra of B_ql. Exact finite equivariance is J_F(alpha_s^F(weak-int f(t)alpha_t^F(W_xi)dt))=G_F(xi,tau_s f). Passing through the uniform all-shape limits defines theta_sp,s G(xi,f)=G(xi,tau_s f). For a pre-embedded finite polynomial tilde(P)_F in B(H_F), put P_F=J_F(tilde(P)_F) and P_F^s=J_F(alpha_s^F(tilde(P)_F)). Isometry of J_F and alpha_s^F gives ||P_F^s||=||P_F||. Consequently the zero-limit kernel is shift invariant, theta_sp,s is isometric, and theta_sp,-s is its inverse. On generators, ||theta_sp,s G(xi,f)-G(xi,f)||<=||tau_s f-f||_1->0. Density, contractivity and the group law extend this to a point-norm C0 automorphism group theta_sp on B_sp. On the cofinal periodic v4.0 path, the compatible exact field inversions Gamma_L commute with the zero-source dynamics and send G_(P_L)(xi,f) to G_(P_L)(-xi,f). Periodic norm convergence and isometry of Gamma_L show that G(xi,f)->G(-xi,f) preserves the zero-limit kernel and norm. It therefore defines an isometric involution gamma_sp with gamma_sp theta_sp,s=theta_sp,s gamma_sp; no parity premise on every auxiliary boundary background is needed. On the C_c^1-kernel formal orbit-smear star algebra, send each formal A_(xi,f) to G(xi,f) and extend by products, stars and linearity. This algebra is dense in the R-167 v1.6 carrier A_H^0 because C_c^1(R) is dense in L1(R) and ||A_(xi,f)||_H<=||f||_1. Because the periodic exact-Q3 backgrounds belong to the same comparison, their supremum representation norm gives ||q_sp,0(a)||<=||a||_H on the dense formal algebra. The map extends uniquely to a contractive unital star-homomorphism q_sp:A_H^0->B_sp. A C-star homomorphism has closed image, while the generator images are dense by the definition of B_sp; hence q_sp is surjective. The finite shift and parity identities pass to q_sp theta_s=theta_sp,s q_sp and q_sp gamma=gamma_sp q_sp. This is a quotient onto one spatial quasi-local subalgebra. It does not turn temporally smeared generators into a seed-indexed commuting local net and does not place raw unsmeared oscillator Weyl elements in a point-norm C0 full-Hamiltonian algebra. For every formal star-polynomial a, the same-net periodic backgrounds obey ||J_L pi_L^0(a)-q_sp(a)||->0 along the R-167 v4.0 volume path. For a in A_H^0 choose formal a_n with ||a-a_n||_H->0. Contractivity and the representation bound give limsup_L||J_L pi_L^0(a)-q_sp(a)||<=2||a-a_n||_H; then n->infinity. Thus the norm convergence holds for every completed a. If k is in ker(q_sp), the isometry of J_L gives ||pi_L^0(k)||=||J_L pi_L^0(k)||->0 along the same periodic net. This same-net conclusion is the load-bearing bridge to the v4.0 states. R-167 v4.0 supplies along one joint subsequence the diagonal source-ground pullbacks omega_L^sigma on A_H^0 converging weak-star to theta-ground states omega_sigma, with omega_-=omega_+ o gamma and one fixed contractive odd witness b. For k in ker(q_sp), omega_sigma(k^*k)=lim_L omega_L^sigma(k^*k)<=lim_L||pi_L^0(k)||^2=0. Cauchy-Schwarz makes ker(q_sp) null for omega_sigma. Surjectivity therefore gives unique states bar(omega)_sigma on B_sp satisfying omega_sigma=bar(omega)_sigma o q_sp. The GNS representation of omega_sigma factors through q_sp. Equivariance leaves the same implementing unitary group and nonnegative generator, so bar(omega)_sigma is a theta_sp-ground state. Parity descends as bar(omega)_-=bar(omega)_+ o gamma_sp. With d>0 from v4.0, bar(omega)_+(q_sp(b))>=d/2 and bar(omega)_-(q_sp(b))<=-d/2; hence ||bar(omega)_+-bar(omega)_-||>=d and q_sp(b)!=0.

assertions.actual: R-167 v4.2 is conditional on summable integrated-toggle weights uniform over intermediate backgrounds, boundary histories, insertion orders, compact time shifts and both time orientations; it does not prove those weights for exact Q3. It proves an all-shape Cauchy limit only for integrated orbit smears and their star-polynomials, a point-norm C0 action on the resulting spatial subalgebra B_sp, a surjective equivariant quotient q_sp from A_H^0, same-net kernel annihilation, and transfer of only the R-167 v4.0 diagonal ground pair and fixed witness. B_sp is not proved to be a seed-indexed commuting local net or the raw oscillator algebra. There is no identification with EXP-000790, EXP-000781 DLR states, v3.8 KMS states or v3.4 Yarotskii branches, and no GNS spectral gap, purity, factoriality, disjointness, phase exhaustion, regulator removal, continuum, mass gap, physical vacuum, empty-space comparison, Round-1, C6, CP1, physical Sector A or Pre-A closure. All five active parent gates and both historical gates remain OPEN. No new negative result is registered.
